name: RT9742SNGV
title: 70mΩ/55mΩ, 3A/2.5A/2A/1.5A/1A/0.5A high-side power switches with flag
summary: The RT9742 family are single N-MOSFET high-side switches for USB power, running from 2.7 V to 6 V with a charge-pumped gate. They limit current, fold back and shut down on heat, lock out at low input, block reverse current and, on versions with a FLG pin, report faults through a deglitched open-drain flag. Versions differ in current rating (0.5 A to 3 A), enable polarity, output discharge and package (TSOT-23-5, TSOT-23-5 (FC), SOT-23-3). RT9742SNGV is the 0.5 A SOT-23-3 version with internal pull-high enable and no discharge.

circuits.title: Simplified application circuit
circuits.description: One switch feeding a USB port. The supply, 2.7 V to 6 V, meets VIN and its bypass capacitor; FLG is pulled up to VIN and goes to the over-current input of the USB controller; the enable line drives EN/E̅N̅. VOUT carries VBUS to the connector with a ceramic and a polarised capacitor across it to ground. D+ and D- pass straight from the connector to the data lines.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, versions with FLG
circuits.description: A USB port switch for the five-pin versions with a fault flag. A 10 µF capacitor bypasses VIN; a 10k to 100k resistor from VIN holds FLG high and the USB controller watches it for over-current. VOUT has 0.1 µF to ground at the chip, then a ferrite bead in VBUS and another in the ground return lead to the connector, where a polarised bulk capacitor sits across VBUS and ground. The A, C, E, G, N, Q and U versions turn on with a high enable; B, D, F, H, P and R with a low one.

parts.value: Chip enable: rising edge turns on A/C/E/G/N/Q/U, falling edge B/D/F/H/P/R

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, SOT-23-3 versions
circuits.description: The three-pin versions, J, K, L and S, have no enable or flag pin; the enable is pulled high inside. VIN takes 10 µF to ground; VOUT takes 0.1 µF at the chip, then passes through a ferrite bead to the connector's VBUS, with a second bead in the ground lead and a polarised bulk capacitor across the connector side.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, RT9742M/V
circuits.description: The M and V versions in TSOT-23-5 have two VOUT pins and an active-high EN, and no flag. VIN takes 10 µF; VOUT takes 0.1 µF at the chip and runs through a ferrite bead to the USB connector, a second bead sits in the ground lead, and a further capacitor stands across VBUS and ground at the connector.

circuits.title: USB power switch application circuit
circuits.description: A 5 V USB downstream port. VIN is bypassed by CIN; a 10k pull-up from VIN keeps FLG high and the USB controller reads it as its over-current signal. VOUT has 0.1 µF at the chip; ferrite beads in VBUS and in the ground return separate it from 120 µF at the port connector, the bulk value USB asks for on downstream-facing ports of a hub.

operation.text: The pass device is a single N-MOSFET between VIN (drain) and VOUT (source). An internal charge pump lifts the gate drive above the source, and a driver sets the gate voltage. On-resistance is 55 mΩ typical in TSOT-23-5 (FC) and 70 mΩ in TSOT-23-5 and SOT-23-3.

Output current is sensed all the time. On an overload or a short the driver pulls the gate down so the MOSFET runs in saturation and the output becomes a constant current source at ILIM; this lasts until the fault clears or thermal shutdown acts. A short can draw a brief large current before the limit responds. The over-current trip threshold ITRIP, measured with a 100 A/s ramp, is always above ILIM on the same part.
When the junction reaches about 140°C the switch turns off; it turns back on once the junction has cooled to 120°C (20°C hysteresis).
The switch stays off until VIN rises past 2.4 V, and turns off again if VIN falls below the threshold (0.1 V hysteresis typical). The lockout is active only while the switch is enabled.

EN (active high) or E̅N̅ (active low), by version, turns the switch and the internal circuits off when inactive. A floating enable gives unpredictable behaviour, and EN must not go below GND. Tying the enable to VIN, or to GND for the active-low versions, keeps the switch on. SOT-23-3 versions have the enable pulled high inside. Turn-on from enable to 90% of VOUT is 2.1 ms typical, and the 10% to 90% rise 1.5 ms.

FLG is an open-drain N-channel output. It goes low on current limit or on a die temperature above about 140°C, and sinks 10 mA at about 200 mV. Over-current reporting waits out the delay tD, 10 ms typical, so inrush into a large capacitive load at hot plug does not raise a false fault. FLG needs a pull-up; a high value saves power, and 100 kΩ suits most designs.

When enabled the MOSFET conducts both ways, so current flows from VOUT to VIN if VOUT is higher. The switch has no body diode: disabled, it blocks current from a VOUT forced above VIN. A reverse-voltage circuit turns the switch off once VOUT exceeds VIN by VREV, 200 mV typical, and turns it on again when VOUT falls back to the level of VIN.

Controlled rise and fall times limit inrush when a large capacitive load is plugged in, keeping the upstream supply droop within USB limits. Versions with the discharge function (Discharge = Yes in the ordering table) pull VOUT down through about 100 Ω while disabled.

The output can carry up to the current limit over the full junction temperature range, but the current must be derated at high ambient so the junction stays at or below 125°C. Allowed dissipation is flat up to 25°C ambient and falls linearly to zero at 125°C.

Use a 10 µF low-ESR ceramic from VIN to GND at the part to stop the input sagging during hot plug; more capacitance reduces the sag further. Without it, ringing from source lead inductance after an output short can destroy the control circuitry. Input transients must stay below the 7 V absolute maximum.

For USB, each downstream port needs at least 120 µF to hold the VBUS drop to 330 mV. Too much output capacitance raises inrush at turn-on and the VIN spike at an output short, so 120 µF to 330 µF is the recommended range. In general use, 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF of ceramic at the output improves immunity to short-circuit transients.
USB requires at least 4.75 V at a self-powered hub port and 4.40 V at a bus-powered hub port. The USB contact resistance limit is 30 mΩ and the allowed PCB-plus-switch drop is 100 mV.

Put the ceramic input capacitor as close to VIN as possible. Use a ground plane under the circuit, and separate ground and power planes where possible. Keep VBUS traces short, at least 50 mil wide in 2 oz copper. Use few vias, and large ones where needed. Slots in the ground plane between ports reduce transient coupling from one port to the next. Place the beads and the bulk capacitor near the USB connector, and the RT9742 near the output port.
